I work on operations research, optimization, and machine learning — building
algorithms that let complex systems make good decisions on their own. Most of
the applications come from inventory, manufacturing, and supply chain
management, where the environment is uncertain and the decision has to be made
anyway.

<!-- ## Research Directions

**Data-driven optimization for supply chains.** Multi-echelon inventory systems
have to be controlled under demand and lead-time uncertainty. I develop
optimization methods that learn directly from data rather than from an assumed
demand distribution.

**Optimization for robotic manufacturing.** Scheduling and control problems in
flexible automation, where the system configuration itself is part of what gets
optimized.

**Explainable reinforcement learning.** Learned policies tend to be opaque, which
is a problem when a person has to act on their recommendations. I work on
reinforcement learning methods whose decisions can be interpreted — and
therefore trusted — by the people who use them. -->
